category_title: Improving ELL student motivated by practical and interest-based literacy
minimal_context: The student is reviewing daily packets for his Physical Science class to complete outside of the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at your Physical Science assignments. You have these daily packets to complete outside of the classroom.

STUDENT: Well, I’m not the best, but I’m not bad so I would put myself in the middle. I don’t do bad but not great.

TUTOR: Okay, let's just start working on the first packet.

STUDENT: I am receptive to putting forth the effort required, even if it challenges me.

TUTOR: Keep going, you still have a lot of work from these packets to finish outside of the classroom.

STUDENT: (Expresses frustration) I get frustrated with teachers who assign a lot of work outside of the classroom. I often fail the classes in which too much work is assigned.

options.A: Consistently enforce the use of organizational skills for managing the daily packets outside the classroom.
options.B: Gradually increase the amount of assignment activity for the daily packets as the class progresses.
options.C: Allow time in the classroom for individualized study on the packets with a peer tutor or volunteer.
options.D: Use interview prompts and the Academic Volitional Strategy Inventory to measure self-regulated learning strengths and weaknesses.
